sources.query: site:w3.org H58 language attributes OR inline-bidi-markup OR info-and-relationships
sources.takeaway: Confirmed W3C ACT Rule de46e4 and Technique H58 for programmatic language tags on inline and block elements.

sources.title: W3C WAI WCAG 2.1 Technique H58: Using language attributes to identify changes in the human language
sources.takeaway: Sufficient technique for WCAG 2.1 SC 3.1.2: every element whose content language differs from the inherited document language must carry a valid BCP 47 `lang` attribute (`lang="de"` on German `<code>` spans and German `.option-text` choices).

sources.title: W3C WAI ACT Rule de46e4: Element with lang attribute has valid language tag
sources.takeaway: Elements with non-empty `lang` attributes must use known primary language subtags (`de`, `ar`) and contain non-empty human-language text inheriting its programmatic language.

sources.title: W3C Internationalization: Inline markup and bidirectional text in HTML
sources.takeaway: Tightly wrap opposite-direction inline phrases with `dir="ltr" lang="de"` when known to be German, and use `dir="auto"` on elements with mixed or run-time directional text (`.quiz-feedback`, `.performance-task-card p`, `.performance-task-rubric li`, Arabic `<code>` spans).

sources.title: Lingolia German Grammar: Prepositions in German Grammar
sources.takeaway: Verified German prepositions with accusative (`durch, für, gegen, ohne, um`), dative (`aus, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu`), contractions (`beim, im, ins, vom, zum, zur`), causal/reference prepositions (`aufgrund, wegen, bezüglich + Genitiv`, `laut / zufolge + Dativ`) used in B2.8–B2.12.
